name: Hubstaff
tagline: Track opt-in work time without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 owner seat; 100 screenshots/user/month; 500 to-dos; 3 clients; no scheduled reports; 1 free organization/account.
tiers.notes: Permanent free plan documented in Hubstaff's official plan guide; separate from the 14-day paid-plan trial.

tiers.name: Small Business Essentials
tiers.limits: 3 paid seats + the owner free (4 members total); 3 clients; unlimited screenshots and app/URL tracking; no add-ons.
tiers.notes: $144/year paid upfront; annual only; offered to qualifying new small organizations.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 2-seat minimum; 500 screenshots/user/month; 500 apps + 500 URLs/user/month; 500 to-dos; 5 clients.

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.limits: 2-seat minimum; 1,500 screenshots, 1,500 apps, and 1,500 URLs/user/month; 1,500 to-dos; unlimited clients; 1 integration.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 2-seat minimum; unlimited screenshots, app/URL tracking, and integrations; scheduling, approvals, payroll, and workforce analytics.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 2-seat minimum; enterprise deployment, SSO, SCIM, HIPAA/SOC 2 controls, concierge setup, and 2-hour email support SLA.
tiers.notes: Annual only on the public rate card.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 owner seat; 100 screenshots/user/month; 500 to-dos; 3 clients; no scheduled reports; 1 free organization/account.
pricing.billingTerms: Free plan + annual-only $144 Small Business Essentials + paid per-seat plans with monthly, quarterly, or annual billing; Enterprise annual only; 14-day paid-plan trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid per-seat plans have a 2-seat minimum; everyone except Project Viewers counts, including owners, managers, inactive users, and users with tracking disabled. Add-ons start at $2.50/seat/month for Insights, $2.50 for Tasks, $1.67 for data retention, $2.50 for more screenshots, $3.33 for Locations, and $2.50 for Silent App. Monthly added seats are charged for the full cycle; quarterly/annual additions are prorated; removed seats receive no credit or refund. VIP support can add $29 or $99/organization/month.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Hubstaff, track opt-in work time without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring. The hard boundary is workforce tracking, payroll, gps, scheduling, reports, and compliance operations, plus ubiquitous capture, coaching, and team workflow.
coreLoopDIY: Track opt-in work time and focused sessions without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring, review patterns locally, and export a transparent activity record.
requirements: optional accessibility permission for app-name tracking
whatYouLose: workforce tracking, payroll, GPS, scheduling, reports, and compliance operations
moatNotes: ubiquitous capture, coaching, and team workflow
ongoingBurden: idle detection, permissions, app metadata, privacy, notifications, sync, reports, integrations, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Hubstaff because the timer is simple, but people pay for frictionless capture and a history they trust enough to invoice or change habits from. The recurring cost buys idle detection, permissions, app metadata, privacy, notifications, sync, reports, integrations, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Kimai
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source time-tracking application with projects, reports, and exports.

alternatives.name: Clockify Free
alternatives.desc: Five users get timers and a private auto-tracker; reports stop at 31-day windows and CSV export is paid.

facts.install: Create a hosted workspace and use the web, desktop, mobile, or browser-extension clients
facts.dataFormat: Time entries, projects, clients, and workspace records live in Clockify's cloud; desktop auto-tracker observations are collected locally before selected items are turned into time entries
facts.gapVsPaid: Clockify Free lacks Hubstaff’s timesheet approvals, scheduling, payroll workflow, unrestricted report history, and included export controls.

alternatives.name: Kimai
alternatives.desc: Timesheets, rates, reports and invoices are all there; approvals need its free plugin and the server still needs an adult.

facts.install: Use Kimai Cloud or deploy the free edition on a server with Docker or the manual PHP/Composer installer
facts.dataFormat: Timesheets, users, customers, projects, rates, and invoice data live in the Kimai database on Kimai Cloud or the user's server, with generated files and uploads on that host
facts.gapVsPaid: Kimai is strong for timesheets and invoices but lacks Hubstaff’s polished native automatic tracker, mobile and GPS workflow, and integrated payroll operations.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires a maintained server, database, Docker or a supported PHP stack, plus backups and reverse-proxy/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: solidtime
alternatives.desc: Modern multi-user timers, clients and billable rates in one Compose stack; the desktop apps are still beta.

facts.install: Create a managed account or deploy the official Docker Compose self-hosting stack
facts.dataFormat: Users, organizations, projects, clients, and time entries live in PostgreSQL, with application state in persistent Docker volumes, on solidtime's service or the user's host
facts.gapVsPaid: solidtime’s desktop clients remain less mature and its approvals, scheduling, payroll, and management reporting are much thinner than Hubstaff’s.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, environment and application keys, mail configuration, persistent storage, migrations, and a reverse proxy with TLS

alternatives.name: Super Productivity
alternatives.desc: Projects, timesheets, reports and break reminders live in one local app; no manager surveillance dashboard attached.

facts.install: Use the browser/PWA or install a packaged desktop or mobile build
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, projects, time records, and settings are local-first in browser or app storage; optional synchronization and backups use the user's chosen WebDAV or Dropbox account
facts.gapVsPaid: Super Productivity is a single-user local productivity app rather than a manager-facing system for team approvals, payroll, schedules, and consolidated reporting.

alternatives.name: TimeCamp Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited people and projects get timers, auto-tracking and a personal activity timeline; app analytics and approvals are paid.

facts.install: Create a hosted account and use the browser, desktop, mobile, or extension clients
facts.engines: TimeCamp's proprietary AI Time Tracking Agent and AI time-entry suggestions; the underlying model provider is not disclosed on the checked official pages
facts.dataFormat: Time entries, projects, users, reports, and optional app/website activity records live in TimeCamp's cloud and synchronize from web, desktop, and mobile clients
facts.gapVsPaid: TimeCamp Free tracks time well but withholds approvals, richer invoicing, payroll workflow, and management analytics that Hubstaff provides.
facts.setupBlocker: Basic timers need no special setup; automatic activity tracking requires installing the desktop agent and granting it activity-monitoring permissions

alternatives.name: TimeTagger
alternatives.desc: A lean timeline, tags and PDF or CSV reports in one container; it is built for individuals, not payroll departments.

facts.install: Use the paid hosted service or run the free Docker Compose image or Python package on your own server
facts.dataFormat: Time records and settings live in TimeTagger's database files on a persistent self-hosted volume or its hosted service; the browser keeps an offline cache that later synchronizes
facts.gapVsPaid: TimeTagger is designed mainly for individual time logging and lacks Hubstaff’s team approvals, payroll, scheduling, and administrative controls.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires Docker or Python hosting, persistent storage, hashed credentials, and HTTPS through a reverse proxy

alternatives.name: Toggl Track Free
alternatives.desc: Five users get fast timers, projects, tags and reports; approvals and paid-time controls cost extra.

facts.install: Create a hosted workspace and use the web, desktop, mobile, or browser-extension clients
facts.dataFormat: Time entries, projects, clients, tags, and team records live in Toggl's cloud and synchronize from online or offline clients; reports can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Toggl Track Free omits approvals, billable-rate controls, project tasks, and management permissions that Hubstaff teams commonly need.

alternatives.name: Traggo
alternatives.desc: A tiny tag-based timer with useful dashboards in one container; invoices and mobile apps never arrive.

facts.install: Run the official Docker container or standalone server binary and mount a persistent data directory
facts.dataFormat: Users, tags, targets, dashboards, and time spans live in a SQLite database in the server's persistent data directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Traggo has no native mobile apps, invoices, approvals, payroll workflow, or scheduling comparable to Hubstaff.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server or Docker, persistent storage, an immediate change from the default administrator password, and a reverse proxy with TLS for public access

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a personal desktop tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Hubstaff in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and optional OS accessibility APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track opt-in work time and focused sessions without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring, review patterns locally, and export a transparent activity record.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create one-click start and stop, manual entries, idle detection, tags, projects, and notes.
Keep any application-name tracking opt-in and never record window contents or keystrokes.
Add Pomodoro-style focus sessions, break reminders, and an optional allowlist blocker.
Provide daily, weekly, project, and category reports with editable corrections.
Export CSV and JSON and make the underlying event log inspectable.
Add automatic local backups and a privacy screen explaining every collected field.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out employee surveillance.
Deliberately leave out payroll and billing automation.
Deliberately leave out cross-device blocking and behavioral coaching services.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
